<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>Story 9.2 is implemented in `D:\Projects\Office\pre-sales-agent-92`. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Test results** (all against `psa_test92`, which I created; both DB URLs point at `127.0.0.1`):
- The spec's targeted backend command passes (324 tests).
- Full backend suite: 2473 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `tests/test_tool_gateway.py::test_every_action_has_one_category_and_every_tool_is_a_read`, and it was already broken on main: `reviews.review_request.create` and `reviews.review_request.cancel` (from 9.1) were never given a permission category in `ACTION_CATEGORIES`. My new action has one. I left it alone because picking "send" or "write" for those two is your call; it's a one-line fix.
- ruff and mypy are clean on `app` and `scripts`.
- Web: `npm run typecheck`, `npx eslint src` and `npm test` all pass (2115 tests). Prettier was not run.
- The migration upgrades, downgrades and upgrades again cleanly.

**Backend**
- **New `notifications` module.** It has the table, a channel port with the one in-app adapter, and `notify()`, which writes an item once per dedupe key and returns whether it wrote one. The four `/api/v1/inbox` endpoints are there; another user's item returns 404. Each item's status and link are read live from the module that owns its subject.
- **Producers**, each in the producer's own transaction:
  - Review Request created and cancelled.
  - A run waiting on a decision; the item goes to whoever started the run.
  - A Conflict escalation.
- **Reminders.** A daily `reviews.send_reminders` job sends one reminder per elapsed interval. It writes the new `reviews.review_request.reminded` trace event only when an item was actually created, so a rerun on the same day sends nothing. The interval is the new `PSA_REVIEW_REMINDER_DAYS` setting (default 3).
- **Migration `20261025_0048_notifications.py`.** It creates the table without delete rights for the app role, seeds the daily schedule, and back-fills pending requests, open decisions on waiting runs, and escalated Conflicts using the same keys the live code uses.
- **Wiring:**
  - the new action `notifications.notification.read`, granted to every role and added to `seed_auth0.py`;
  - import-linter contracts (19, all kept);
  - `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md`, `README.md`, `.env.example` and the worker env in `compose.yaml`.

**Web**
- **Inbox page.** It is built to the mockup:
  - grouped list next to a detail card;
  - selecting a row marks it read;
  - j/k, Enter and arrow-key navigation;
  - Previous/Next pages, the skeleton, the empty state and Mark all read.
- **Sidebar badge.** It shares one count with the Inbox page, refreshes on focus and every 30 s, and listens to the Opportunity's stream when you're inside one.
- **Supporting changes.** `schema.d.ts` was regenerated against a fresh local uvicorn (additions only). I moved `parsePage` into `lib/pagination.ts`, because importing it from the server-only `data.ts` broke the page tests. Four existing test files now mock the Inbox server actions so they can render the shell.

**Things to check:**
- **Back-fill summaries may differ slightly.** For Assessment targets, migration-written summaries can word things slightly differently from live ones, because the migration builds them in SQL. Dedupe uses the key, not the text, so nothing is duplicated.
- **Re-raised escalated Conflicts.** When a later run re-raises one, the old item follows the chain to the newest Conflict's status, so it stays open.
- **Links go through `/inbox`.** Opening an item from the Inbox works, but someone who has since lost access to the Opportunity will get a 404 there.
- **Choices the spec didn't settle:**
  - The detail pane starts empty ("Select an item to see it here.") instead of auto-selecting the first row, so nothing is marked read without a click.
  - I wrote the detail-pane sentences and the waiting-run and Conflict summary texts myself.
- **Not done:** I haven't updated the Obsidian demo-plan note.</result>

- **The Inbox sorts by group before time, so new items that need action fall off page 1.** `page_of` orders by `_GROUP_RANK` first, then `created_at desc`, over the recipient's whole history. Rows are never deleted, and read or closed items are never pushed down. Over time, every old Review Request item (cancelled, decided or superseded, already read) sits above a run or escalated Conflict that arrived today. A user with 30 old review items will find a fresh "Conflict escalated" item on page 2. Put unread or open items first, or sort only open subjects by group. The `(recipient_id, read_at, created_at)` index also can't serve the `CASE` sort, so every page read sorts all of the recipient's rows.

- **Runs that the system started notify no one.** `_notify_starter` returns early when `run_starter` is None. The workflows public docstring says `enqueue_run` is called by `gaps` after a Gap detection, which is a system start. In that path, a run paused in `waiting_for_human` creates no Inbox item for anyone, and the migration back-fill skips it the same way. There is no fallback recipient, such as the Opportunity owner, and no test of a system-started run.

- **Opportunity titles are shown without checking that the recipient can still see the Opportunity.** `_items` calls `opportunities.opportunity_titles` with "no authorization". Cancelling a review revokes the reviewer's read access, yet that reviewer's Inbox keeps showing the live `opportunity_title`, including any later renames. The `itemBody` text and the row meta repeat it. Items for Opportunities the caller can no longer read should drop the title, or show the stored summary only.

- **Unread counts include items that need nothing.** When a request is cancelled, the reviewer gets two unread items: the original `review_requested` and the `review_cancelled` update. The test asserts `_unread == 2`. The original request item stays unread in "Review Requests" with no link. Items whose subject has closed are never marked read automatically and are not excluded from the count, so the badge grows with items that need no action.

- **Changing `PSA_REVIEW_REMINDER_DAYS` silently skips or misnumbers reminders.** The reminder key is `review:{id}:reminder:{N}` and does not record the interval length. Suppose the setting goes from 1 day to 3. At day 6, N = 2, but `reminder:2` was already written on day 2 under the 1-day setting, so no reminder goes out. Include the interval in the key (for example `reminder:{days}d:{N}`), or key on the due date. No test covers a settings change.

- **Moving through the list with the arrow keys or j/k marks every row passed as read.** `onKeyDown` calls `select(target)`, and `select` marks the item read. The test even asserts that `markInboxItemRead` is called twice just from arrowing. A keyboard user who scans the list loses unread state for items they never looked at. Mouse users only mark read on click. Move focus on arrow keys and mark read only on an explicit select (Enter or click), or after a dwell time.

- **After a failed first load, the Inbox reloads page 1 whatever page the URL asks for.** `pageNumber = initial?.page ?? 1`. If `/inbox?page=3` fails on the server, `initial` is null, and the focus or 30-second `reload` then fetches page 1 while the URL still says page 3. The Pagination links then work from page 1. Pass the parsed `page` from `page.tsx` as a prop instead of deriving it from `initial`.

- **Optimistic mark-read never rolls back, and a poll can overwrite it.** `select` sets `read: true` and lowers `unread` before the server call. If `markInboxItemRead` returns `error` or `not-found`, the local state is never restored. A `reload` (focus or 30-second poll) that started before the mark-read lands can also bring back `read: false` until the next poll, so the row flickers. Nothing tests the error path.

- **Polling never pauses for hidden tabs, and each Inbox poll is expensive.** `useInboxRefresh` sets a 30-second `setInterval` with no `document.visibilityState` check. The sidebar badge (on every page) and `InboxView` (on `/inbox`) each poll, so every background tab keeps sending server actions. Each Inbox poll then runs `_subject` once per item, one at a time: 25 or more lookups, plus a loop of `successor_of` queries for each Conflict item. Skip polls while the tab is hidden, and batch the subject-status lookups by `subject_type`.

- **The reminder job sends everything in one unbounded transaction.** `send_due_reminders` loads every pending request older than one interval, with no limit. It calls `target_labels`, which runs `_current_assessments` once per Opportunity, then fetches titles and appends trace events, all in a single UoW. The docstring calls it "one short Unit of Work". One failure rolls back every reminder, and with `max_attempts=3` the job repeats the whole batch. The first run after deploy also sends reminders for every old pending request at once, because the back-fill writes no reminder rows. Neither behaviour is documented or tested.

- **Live and back-filled summaries can differ for Assessment targets.** The live `target_labels` names only current assessment snapshots (`_current_assessments`). A request for a non-current assessment falls back to `"Assessment v{n}"`. The migration joins `assessments_assessments` by id and always writes `"{Agent} Assessment v{n}"`. The same request can therefore get different summaries depending on whether its item was back-filled or written live. The back-fill test covers only Estimate targets.

On the web side, `OTHER_STATUSES` repeats them again. A new Conflict or decision status would show as unknown or be treated as closed without any failing test. Have `conflict_status` and `decision_status` return an `is_open` flag and a label from the owning module, as `reviews` does with `STATUS_LABELS`.

async def enqueue_run(uow: UnitOfWork, opportunity_id: UUID) -> UUID:
    """Queue an assessment run of the Opportunity in the caller's Unit of Work, as the
    system, unless one of its runs is already queued, running or waiting for a person: then
    that run's id is returned and nothing added (a running run keeps the inputs it read; a
    waiting one is not rebuilt until someone resolves it). Lost runs are
    failed first. Never refuses with a conflict; any other error (e.g. the database) fails
    the caller's Unit of Work."""
    await repo.lock_runs(uow, opportunity_id)
    await fail_stale(uow, opportunity_id)
    ids = {"opportunity_id": str(opportunity_id)}
    active = await repo.run_active(uow, opportunity_id)
    if active is not None:
        _log.info("workflows.run_coalesced", extra={**ids, "run_id": str(active)})
        return active
    run_id = await queue_run(uow, opportunity_id, SYSTEM)
    _log.info("workflows.run_queued", extra={**ids, "run_id": str(run_id)})
    return run_id

The `IS NOT NULL` guard keeps out NULL recipients, and owner IDs are required anyway. `_summary` matches `clean_summary` and `decision_summary`. One small difference: an empty-string title gives `"head â€”"` in SQL but `"head"` in Python. That only matters if titles can be empty.

**3. `inbox-view.tsx`: two defects, both from moving the page's count by a fixed delta.**

A mark-read reply that resolves at that moment hits this, and the badge stays stale until the next poll. Fix: clear it inside the async body, `try { do {â€¦} while (again) } finally { inFlight = null; }`. <result>I've implemented Story 9.3 in the worktree `D:\Projects\Office\pre-sales-agent-93` (branch `task/story-9-3-review-decisions`), with nothing committed or pushed. All the test runs pass on `psa_test93`, including the full backend suite. The one thing I couldn't check is that the new "Open in tab" page route leaves the existing Estimate tab URL working (see the risks below).

No rebase was needed: the branch was already at `origin/main` with 9.2 (PR #89) merged. Your local `main` is behind `origin/main`.

**Backend**
- **Decisions table:** migration `20261026_0049_reviews_review_decisions.py` (revision `0049`, after 9.2's `0048`) adds `reviews_review_decisions`. The database enforces the rules: a reason is required for everything except an approval, a reason is at most 1,000 characters, and an escalation must name who it goes to. The app role can only read and insert rows. The same migration adds `approved` and `rejected` to the version status check, and the downgrade maps both back to `in_review`. It upgrades, downgrades and passes `alembic check`.
- **Recording a decision:** new `reviews/domain/decisions.py` and `reviews/application/decisions.py` run the steps in the order the spec gives and produce every effect it lists. The routes are `POST â€¦/decisions` and `GET â€¦/panel`, and every request list now carries its latest decision.
- **Version statuses:** `estimates` gains `approved` and `rejected`, and both stay current until a newer version supersedes them. It also gains `mark_approved`, `mark_rejected`, `version_detail`, and a new `compare.py` with `compare_versions`, which matches lines by section and title.
- **Panel for an Assessment:** `assessments` gains `assessment_at`, so the panel can show an Assessment at the reviewed version.
- **Wiring:** new action and grants, two new 403 error codes (`reviewer_not_authorized`, `self_approval_forbidden`), three trace events, and the table added to `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md`.
- **Inbox:** an item is now closed, with status "Escalated" and no **Open**, once the reader is no longer the request's reviewer.

**Web**
- New `review-panel.tsx` holds the panel, laid out as the mockup's review block. It opens in three places:
  - in the Inspector, from a Review requests row or a `?review=` link;
  - in the Inbox detail card, in place of the old body and **Open**;
  - full width at the new page `app/opportunities/[id]/estimate/reviews/[rid]/page.tsx`.
- The card's status pill shows the latest decision, the version pills use the resolved and blocker colours, and the lifecycle shows Approved as current.
- `schema.d.ts` was regenerated from a fresh dump of the backend's API schema.

**Verification**
- **Backend story tests:** the six files the spec lists, plus the Inbox and tool-gateway tests, pass (368 tests). `test_reviews_decisions.py` covers every row of the spec's table plus the other checks it asks for.
- **Full backend suite:** 2,506 passed and 1 failed. The failure was the new action having no permission category. I classed it as an approval, and the test now passes.
- **Lint and types:** ruff, mypy and import-linter are clean.
- **Web:** `npm run typecheck`, `npx eslint src` and `npm test` pass (140 files, 2,158 tests, with axe checks on every panel state).

**Decisions and risks to review**
- **Owner can decide:** I also gave the decide action to Opportunity owners, which the spec doesn't list. Otherwise an owner named as reviewer (allowed when they didn't author the version) could never decide. Only the current reviewer can actually decide either way.
- **Approving an approved version:** sending a review request for it returns `estimate_version_not_submitted` with "v3 is already approved". The spec doesn't say what should happen here.
- **Escalation conflict:** escalating to someone who already has the same pending request returns 409 `review_request_duplicate`, which the spec doesn't mention. Without it the database's one-pending-request rule would make it fail with a 500.
- **Route not verified:** I couldn't confirm in a browser that the new `estimate/reviews/[rid]` folder doesn't stop `/opportunities/{id}/estimate` reaching the existing tab page, because the login redirect runs first. Next.js should still route it to the tab page, but click through once to be sure.
- **Escalation candidates:** the reviewer list is capped at 50 people, sorted by name.
- **Housekeeping:** I ran `npm ci` in the worktree's `web/`. `next dev` generated `web/AGENTS.md` and `web/CLAUDE.md`, which I deleted. I ticked the spec's task checkboxes.
- **Not done:** I didn't update the Obsidian demo-plan note.</result>

    body = client.get(BASE, headers=headers, params={"scope": "mine", "page_size": 200}).json()
    return {item["id"]: item for item in body["items"]}


def test_submitting_a_newer_version_supersedes_one_in_review(
    client: TestClient, sync_engine: Engine
) -> None:
    headers, owner_id = _user(client, sync_engine, "Owner Person", PSE)
    _, ana = _user(client, sync_engine, "Ana Reviewer", ENG)
    opp = _create(client, headers)
    v1 = _version(sync_engine, opp["id"], 1, created_by=owner_id)
    assert _send(client, headers, opp["id"], v1, 1, [ana]).status_code == 201
    assert _status(sync_engine, v1) == "in_review"
    v2 = _version(sync_engine, opp["id"], 2, status="draft", created_by=owner_id)

    submitted = client.post(
        f"{BASE}/{opp['id']}/estimate/versions/{v2}/submit",
        headers={**headers, "If-Match": '"1"'},
    )

    assert submitted.status_code == 200, submitted.text
    assert submitted.json()["superseded_count"] == 1
    assert (_status(sync_engine, v1), _status(sync_engine, v2)) == ("superseded", "submitted")

The spec says the API decides and the UI only reflects its flags. `decide()` should apply the same superseded/missing-version check and return 409. No test posts a decision against a superseded version; `test_a_superseded_version_has_a_read_only_panel` only checks the panel.
- **Diff lines are matched by section and title, not by line key as the spec says.** The spec says to match lines "by catalogue item / line key". `compare.py` matches on `(section, title.strip().casefold())`. If someone renames a line between versions, or moves it to another section, it shows up as one line removed and another added. A changed hours delta is never shown for it. The docstring documents the deviation, but the frozen intent doesn't allow it.
- **Duplicate titles break the web diff list.** `diff_lines` deliberately pairs lines that share a key by position. Several diff rows can therefore have the same `change`, `section` and `title`. `DiffView` in `review-panel.tsx` uses exactly that combination as the React `key`. Duplicate keys cause warnings and can render the wrong rows. The key should include an index or position.
- **The UI can't send a reason with Approve.** The API, the DB check and the spec all allow an optional reason on Approve. In the panel, Approve sends `onDecide("approved", "")` immediately, with no reason field and no confirm step. Approval can't be undone and can move the whole version to `approved`, so one stray click is permanent. There's also no way to leave a note.
- **The Inbox "Escalated" status is decided by "reader isn't the reviewer", not by an actual escalation.** In `notifications/application/inbox.py`, every pending Review item whose `recipient_id != reviewer_id` gets the "Escalated" status and loses its link. That's wrong for any Review-subject item sent to someone who was never the reviewer, such as the author-side items 9.4 will add. Check for an `escalated` decision instead, or limit the rule to `review_requested`/reminder kinds. There's also no test for an item whose recipient was never the reviewer.
- **Deciding from the Inbox doesn't update the Inbox.** `Detail` renders `ReviewPanelLoader` with `live={false}` and no `onDecided`. After Approve, Reject or Escalate there, the list row keeps its old open status until the 30-second poll. Either refresh the item or the list on decide, or update the item's subject status locally.
- **The reason text carries over when the reviewer switches action.** In `DecisionActions`, `choose()` changes the action but leaves `reason` as it was. Text typed under "Reason for rejecting" can be confirmed as an escalation or an evidence request without being retyped. Either reset the reason when the action changes, or keep a separate draft per action.
- **Escalate has no empty state.** When `escalation_candidates` is empty (no one else holds the role), the Select shows only the "Choose a reviewer" placeholder, and Confirm stays disabled with no explanation. Show a line like "No other {type} reviewer is available" and/or disable Escalate.
- **The candidate list can be cut short.** `_candidates` calls `search_users_with_role(..., "", limit=SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT)` and returns at most that many people, with no search box and no "more" flag. In a large org some valid reviewers will never appear in the picker.
- **Decision times are shown in UTC with no label.** `DATE_TIME` and `DATE` in `lib/reviews.ts` hard-code `timeZone: "UTC"`. "Ana Reviewer Â· Evidence requested Â· 25 Oct, 10:02" will be hours off for most users, and nothing says it's UTC.
- **The "Superseded by v4" link doesn't go to v4.** The spec asks for a link "to that version". The panel links to `tabHref(opportunityId, "estimate")`, which is just the current Estimate tab.
- **The Challenge hint is only visible to screen readers.** The spec says Challenge shows as `aria-disabled` "with the hint 'Challenge arrives with Story 9.5'". The hint is in a `sr-only` span, so sighted users see a greyed-out button with no explanation. The author-lock hint, by contrast, is visible.
- **`version_status` is a bare string that uses `""` for unknown.** `RecordedDecision.version_status` and `ReviewPanel.version_status` are typed `str`. That throws away the `VersionStatus` enum in OpenAPI and the generated TS. It also forces `recorded.version_status || panel.version_status` in `afterDecision` and string comparisons in `isSupersededPanel`. Use `VersionStatus | None`.
- **Validation order differs from the spec's numbered steps.** `_clean_reason` (422) runs before the pending check (409) and the If-Match check (412/428). A blank reason on an already-decided or stale request returns 422 instead of the 409/412 the matrix lists. The spec orders actor, then state, then If-Match.
- **A rejected version leaves other reviewers' requests pending.** After one reviewer rejects, the other requests stay pending. Those reviewers keep access, keep getting the 9.2 daily reminders, and can still approve something that can never be approved (as the design note confirms). Nothing tells them, and their panels stay fully actionable. At least pass a "version already rejected" hint into the panel, or stop the reminders.
- **The backend tests have gaps:**
  - Nothing checks that the original reviewer keeps access after escalating when they still have another pending request on the Opportunity (the `has_pending=True` path).
  - Nothing sends a reason over 1,000 characters through the API (it's only tested in the domain), or one over the 4,000-character `REASON_BACKSTOP`.
  - Nothing covers the roll-up for an Assessment-target request (an approval that completes a version with a mix of estimate and assessment requests).
  - Nothing exercises the migration downgrade (approved/rejected mapped back to `in_review`).
- **The adapters docstring now contradicts the new foreign key.** `reviews/adapters/models.py` says the module's tables are "without foreign keys (AD-2)". `ReviewDecisionRow` adds `fk_reviews_review_decisions_review_request_id`. The FK may well be allowed within one module, but the docstring should say so.
- **The status trackers disagree.** The spec front matter says `status: 'in-review'`, while `sprint-status.yaml` moves 9-3 only to `in-progress`. One of them is stale.</result>

async def supersede_drafts(uow: UnitOfWork, opportunity_id: UUID) -> int:
    """Mark the Opportunity's `draft` version `superseded`. Returns how many changed."""
    result = await uow.session.execute(
        update(EstimateVersionRow)
        .where(
            EstimateVersionRow.opportunity_id == opportunity_id,
            EstimateVersionRow.status == "draft",
        )
        .values(status="superseded", row_version=EstimateVersionRow.row_version + 1)
        .returning(EstimateVersionRow.id)
        .execution_options(synchronize_session=False)
    )
    return len(result.all())

async def supersede_submitted(
    uow: UnitOfWork, opportunity_id: UUID, *, keep: UUID
) -> list[VersionRecord]:
    """Mark the Opportunity's `submitted`, `in_review` (Story 9.1), `approved` and `rejected`
    (Story 9.3) versions other than `keep` `superseded` (bumping their `row_version`); the
    versions as they are now, oldest first."""
    result = await uow.session.execute(
        update(EstimateVersionRow)
        .where(
            EstimateVersionRow.opportunity_id == opportunity_id,
            EstimateVersionRow.status.in_(_SENT_STATUSES),
            EstimateVersionRow.id != keep,
        )
        .values(status="superseded", row_version=EstimateVersionRow.row_version + 1)
        .returning(EstimateVersionRow.id)
        .execution_options(synchronize_session=False)
    )
    ids = [row.id for row in result.all()]
    found = [v for i in ids if (v := await get_version(uow, i)) is not None]
    return sorted(found, key=lambda v: v.version)

**Problem:** A reviewer named in a Review Request (9.1) can see the request but can't record a judgement, so no Estimate Version can become `approved` and the Baseline (9.7) stays out of reach.

<result>### A submitted newer version superseding an approved or rejected one is never tested

- **Changed surface:** `_SENT_STATUSES` now includes `approved` and `rejected` (`backend/app/modules/estimates/adapters/repository.py:340`). `supersede_submitted` uses it (`repository.py:441-460`), so submitting a newer draft now supersedes an approved or rejected version. The spec says such a version "stays current and can still be superseded".
- **Impacted consumer or site:** the Story 8.6 submit route, `POST â€¦/estimate/versions/{id}/submit`, which calls `supersede_submitted`.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`.
  - `test_submit_supersedes_the_earlier_submitted_version_and_traces_both` (`backend/tests/test_estimates_submit.py:310`) only supersedes a `submitted` version.
  - `test_submitting_a_newer_version_supersedes_one_in_review` (`backend/tests/test_reviews_requests.py:746`) only supersedes an `in_review` one.
  - In `backend/tests/test_reviews_decisions.py`, the only superseded version is set by a raw SQL `UPDATE` (`test_a_superseded_version_has_a_read_only_panel`).
- **Missing verification:** approve (or reject) v1, insert a v2 draft, submit it, then assert `superseded_count == 1` and that v1 is `superseded`.
- **Demonstration:** if `supersede_submitted` were given its own status tuple without `approved`/`rejected`, an approved v1 would stay `approved`. No test I read would fail.
- **Consequence:** an approved or rejected version could stay non-superseded next to the newly submitted one.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add a parametrized (`approved`, `rejected`) sibling of `test_submitting_a_newer_version_supersedes_one_in_review` in `test_reviews_decisions.py`.

### The rejected-version guard on sending a Review Request lost its `pragma: no cover` but has no test

- **Changed surface:** `_check_reviewable` now raises `EstimateVersionRejectedError` (`estimate_version_rejected`) for a rejected version (`backend/app/modules/reviews/application/requests.py:150-151`). The route docs list this code (`backend/app/modules/reviews/api/routes.py:133`).
- **Impacted consumer or site:** `POST â€¦/review-requests` on an Opportunity whose current version is `rejected`.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. I searched `backend/tests` for `estimate_version_rejected` and `EstimateVersionRejected`. The only hit is the error-to-HTTP mapping row in `test_errors.py`, which never calls `_check_reviewable`. The `approved` branch is reached only by `assert _send(...).status_code == 409` in `test_last_approval_approves_the_version`, which does not check the code.
- **Missing verification:** reject v3, then `_send` on v3 and assert 409 with code `estimate_version_rejected`.
- **Demonstration:** if the rejected branch were dropped or reordered, a rejected version would return 409 `estimate_version_not_submitted` with "not submitted" wording. No test checks the code on this path.
- **Consequence:** the documented error contract for a rejected version can drift without any test noticing.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Extend `test_reject_rejects_the_request_and_the_version` with a send attempt that asserts the code.

### The `decideReviewRequest` server action has no tests

- **Changed surface:** `decideReviewRequest` (`web/src/app/opportunities/actions.ts:3491`) does three things:
  - It trims the reason and sends `null` when it is blank.
  - It sends `escalated_to` only for `escalated`.
  - It sends `If-Match`, then maps 412 to `stale`, 409/422 to `invalid`, 403 to `forbidden` (with no detail when the code is `forbidden`) and 404 to `not-found`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** `ReviewPanelView.decide` (`web/src/components/opportunities/review-panel.tsx`). Its `problemOf` turns `stale` into the "Changed byâ€¦" `InlineAlert` with Reload and View diff.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`.
  - `web/src/app/opportunities/actions.test.ts` tests its 9.1 sibling, `cancelReviewRequest` (lines 2713-2742: request shape plus status mapping), but has no `decideReviewRequest` case.
  - Every other test that touches it mocks the whole module: `review-panel.test.tsx`, `inbox-view.test.tsx`, `estimate-grid.test.tsx`, `pages.test.tsx` and `inbox/page.test.tsx`.
- **Missing verification:** a `decideReviewRequest` block in `actions.test.ts` that asserts the POST path, the `If-Match` header and the body for approve (reason `null`), reject (trimmed reason) and escalate (`escalated_to`). It should also map 412, 409, 422, 403 (`forbidden` and `self_approval_forbidden`) and 404.
- **Demonstration:** some regressions would pass every current test:
  - Mapping 412 to `invalid` would show a plain alert instead of the Reload/View diff alert.
  - Always sending `escalated_to` would make every non-escalate decision fail with 422.
  - Dropping `If-Match` would make every decision fail with 428, which falls through to "not reachable".
- **Consequence:** the 412 handling and the request contract of the main decision call are unprotected.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add the `describe` block to `actions.test.ts`, following the `cancelReviewRequest` tests.

### `ReviewPanelLoader`'s state after a decision is only tested for Approve

- **Changed surface:** `afterDecision` (`web/src/components/opportunities/review-panel.tsx:431`) runs from the loader's `onDecided` (`review-panel.tsx:702`). It does two things:
  - It replaces `request`, which carries the new `row_version` used as the next `If-Match`.
  - It removes the actions when the request is no longer the caller's to decide (`stillMine`: still pending, same reviewer).
- **Impacted consumer or site:** the Inspector, Inbox and Open in tab panels, which all render `ReviewPanelLoader`.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. Only `"reads the panel and keeps the decision without a read"` in `review-panel.test.tsx` goes through `afterDecision`, and it uses an approval, where status â‰  pending already removes the actions. The Escalate and Request evidence tests render `ReviewPanelView` with a mocked `onDecided`, so `afterDecision` never runs for them.
- **Missing verification:**
  - A loader test that escalates and asserts the "Review decision" group is gone.
  - A loader test that requests evidence, then approves, and asserts the second call sends `rowVersion: 2`.
- **Demonstration:** either regression would pass every current test:
  - Dropping the `reviewer.id` comparison would leave Ana's actions showing after she escalates; her next click would get 404 and show "You can't decide this Review Request.".
  - Keeping the old `request` would make a second decision after Request evidence fail with 412.

### The decide path's "has nothing pending left" access check is never tested with a reviewer who still has another request

- **Changed surface:** `decide` revokes the decider's reviewer access using `has_pending=await repo.has_pending_for_reviewer(uow, opportunity_id, decider)` (`backend/app/modules/reviews/application/decisions.py:273-277`). This runs for approve, reject and escalate.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** `opportunities.revoke_reviewer_access`, which decides whether the reviewer can still read the Opportunity and their other pending request.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. In `backend/tests/test_reviews_decisions.py`, every revoking path leaves the decider with no other pending request:

  - `test_partial_approval_waits_for_every_request` asserts only Ben remains, after Ana decides her only request.
  - `test_escalate_hands_the_request_to_another_reviewer` asserts `{cy: reviewer}`.

- **Missing verification:** a reviewer with two pending security requests on one Opportunity approves (or rejects) one. Assert they are still a reviewer collaborator and can still decide the other.
- **Demonstration:** passing `has_pending=False` (or checking pending before `set_status`) in `decide` would revoke Ana's access while her second request is pending. No decisions test would fail.
- **Consequence:** a reviewer could lose access to an Opportunity on which they still owe a decision.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add a two-Assessment-request case to `test_reviews_decisions.py`, using `_assessment` and `_send` as `test_a_reviewer_keeps_access_until_their_last_pending_request_is_cancelled` does.

### The export header labels for approved and rejected versions are untested

- **Changed surface:** `build_export` now takes its header label from `STATUS_LABELS` (`backend/app/modules/estimates/application/export_content.py:24,275`). It adds "Approved" and "Rejected", and falls back to the draft label for any status not in the map.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** the Estimate export, whose header (`document.header[1]`) reads "Estimate vN Â· {label}".
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. `test_a_submitted_version_is_labelled_submitted` (`backend/tests/test_estimates_export_render.py:480-488`) only asserts the `SUBMITTED` label. I found no test of the header for `in_review`, `approved` or `rejected` in `test_estimates_export*.py`.
- **Missing verification:** a test parametrized over `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` that asserts `header[1] == "Estimate v2 Â· Approved"` / `"â€¦ Â· Rejected"`.
- **Demonstration:** dropping an entry from `STATUS_LABELS` would make an approved version export as "Draft â€” not submitted". No test would fail.
- **Consequence:** a client-facing export could mislabel an approved Estimate as a draft.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Parametrize `test_a_submitted_version_is_labelled_submitted` over the sent statuses.

### Nothing checks the migration downgrade's approved/rejected â†’ `in_review` mapping

- **Changed surface:** `downgrade()` in `backend/migrations/versions/20261026_0049_reviews_review_decisions.py:90` sets approved and rejected versions back to `in_review` before restoring the narrower status check.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** the downgrade round trips in other tests, which now pass through 0049: `test_notifications_inbox.py:617` (to 0047) and `test_reviews_requests.py:724` (to 0044).
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. Both round trips run the downgrade, but neither creates an approved or rejected version first or asserts the mapped status. Whether the `UPDATE` is exercised at all depends on leftover rows in the shared test DB.
- **Missing verification:** approve one version and reject another, downgrade to `0048_notifications`, assert both are `in_review`, then upgrade to head.
- **Demonstration:** removing or narrowing the `UPDATE` would pass every test whenever no approved or rejected row happens to be in the DB at downgrade time.
- **Consequence:** a downgrade on real data could fail on the restored check constraint.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add a round trip in `test_reviews_decisions.py` in the style of the downgrade test at `test_reviews_requests.py:724`.

<result>I've fixed all twelve review points. The tests for the files I edited pass (111 backend, 350 web); I didn't rerun the full suites, as you asked.

**Backend**
- **Superseded version:** `decide()` in `reviews/application/decisions.py` now returns 409 `estimate_version_superseded` ("v3 is superseded by v4") before writing anything, right after it loads the version.
- **Cancel after approvals:** in `reviews/application/requests.py`, cancelling the last pending request now approves the version when every other non-cancelled request is approved; otherwise it goes back to `submitted` as before. I updated the docstring to match.
- **Docstring:** `reviews/adapters/models.py` now says there are no cross-module foreign keys and that decisions reference their request.
- **New tests in `tests/test_reviews_decisions.py`:**
  - a decision on a superseded version is refused with nothing written;
  - Ana approves, Ben's request is cancelled, and the version ends up `approved`;
  - for both an approved and a rejected version, submitting a newer draft supersedes it (`superseded_count == 1`);
  - a new request on a rejected version is 409 `estimate_version_rejected`, and on an approved one 409 `estimate_version_not_submitted`;
  - a reviewer with two pending Assessment requests keeps access after deciding the first, decides the second, and only then loses access;
  - downgrading to `0048_notifications` turns an approved and a rejected version back into `in_review`, then upgrade to head.
- **Export header:** `tests/test_estimates_export_render.py` now checks the label for Submitted, In review, Approved and Rejected.

**Web**
- **`review-panel.tsx`:**
  - the diff rows' keys now include the index;
  - switching to another action clears the typed reason and the chosen reviewer;
  - the "Challenge arrives with Story 9.5" hint is now visible, styled like the author hint.
- **`inbox-view.tsx`:** the Review item's panel reloads the Inbox right after a decision, so the row no longer waits for the 30-second poll.
- **`estimate-grid.tsx`:** the `?review=` link now marks itself as opened only when the timer fires, so it still opens under StrictMode in dev.
- **`actions.test.ts`:** a new `decideReviewRequest` block covers:
  - the path and `If-Match` header;
  - a null reason for approve, a trimmed reason for reject, and `escalated_to` only on an escalation;
  - the 412, 409/422, both 403 cases, 404 and 500 mappings;
  - bad input that never reaches the API.
- **`review-panel.test.tsx`:** three new loader tests:
  - the actions disappear after an escalation;
  - Approve after Request evidence sends `rowVersion` 2;
  - switching actions clears the reason.

Ruff, mypy, the web typecheck and eslint on the edited files are clean.</result>

# Product Brief: Agentic AI Presales Platform

**In one line:** a workbench that helps presales engineers find unknown requirements and integration risk *before* committing to a delivery estimate, so that the deals we win are deals we can deliver.

## The Problem

We sell enterprise software as licences plus implementation. We win most of the deals we pursue. Then we find out what they really cost: **delivery estimates usually come in 20â€“50% too low**.

The cause is in how proposals are put together. Opportunities arrive by email, phone call or Teams meeting and pass by hand between sales, presales, engineering, project management, security and commercial. Key customer information is often missing, so people fill gaps with assumptions that never get written down. Each function assesses the deal separately. # Epic 9 Context: Review, Challenge, Baseline and Decision Trace

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Put a qualified human between agent output and any committed figure. Named reviewers approve, reject or challenge a submitted Estimate Version (or specific Assessments). A Challenge reruns only the affected Assessments in a Workflow Run and produces a new Estimate Version with the delta, leaving the challenged version unchanged. Once every requested review is approved and nothing blocks it, the presales engineer sets the Baseline, and only a newer approved version can replace it. Anyone with access can trace any Estimate line or Assumption back to its Findings, Evidence and human decisions through an append-only Decision Trace whose completeness is tested. This closes the R1 loop from "submitted" to "baselined". Status: Story 9.8 is done (demo slice) and 9.1 is in review. Everything else is in the backlog and is built on the Epic 17 redesign.

async def pending_for_reminders(
    uow: UnitOfWork, interval_s: int
) -> tuple[datetime, list[RequestRecord]]:
    """The database's `now()` and the pending requests at least one interval old, oldest
    first (Story 9.2)."""
    now = (await uow.session.execute(select(func.now()))).scalar_one()
    rows = await uow.session.execute(
        select(ReviewRequestRow)
        .where(
            ReviewRequestRow.status == "pending",
            ReviewRequestRow.created_at <= now - timedelta(seconds=interval_s),
        )
        .order_by(ReviewRequestRow.created_at, ReviewRequestRow.id)
        .execution_options(populate_existing=True)
    )
    return now, [_record(row) for row in rows.scalars()]

# Architecture Spine: Agentic AI Presales Platform

## Design Paradigm

**Modular monolith, hexagonal per module.** One Python backend codebase runs as two processes (`api`, `worker`), alongside one Next.js web app. Everything is deployed with Docker Compose on a single Ubuntu GPU VPS, with local models served by Ollama. Each business module has four layers:

| Layer | Directory | May depend on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API (HTTP adapters) | `modules/<m>/api/` | own `application` |
| Application (commands, queries, public interface) | `modules/<m>/application/` | own `domain`, other modules' `application/public.py`, `platform` ports |
| Domain (entities, state machines, rules, ports) | `modules/<m>/domain/` | nothing outside itself |
| Adapters (DB repositories, external systems) | `modules/<m>/adapters/` | own `domain` ports, `platform` |

`orchestration` (LangGraph) and `agents` sit outside the business modules. They drive the modules only through `application/public.py`.

<result>Story 9.4 is implemented in `D:\Projects\Office\pre-sales-agent-94` on branch `task/story-9-4-review-outcomes`, with nothing committed or pushed. Every check passes: the full backend suite on `psa_test94` (2,539 passed, 3 skipped), the spec's targeted backend tests, ruff, mypy, import-linter and `alembic check`, plus web typecheck, eslint and all 2,194 web tests. I didn't open the app in a browser, so I haven't seen the new panels rendered.

**Backend**
- **Migration 0050** (`20261026_0050_review_outcomes.py`):
  - Adds the two new Inbox kinds, `review_outcome` and `review_replied`.
  - Adds `linked_request_id` on Review Requests.
  - Adds the `reviews_review_replies` table, which the app can only read and insert into.
  - The downgrade deletes any items of the new kinds before restoring the old check. I tested down and up.
- **Outcome items:** every decision sends a `review_outcome` item to the Opportunity's owner and the request's sender. When they are the same person they get one item. The summary reads "Ana Reviewer rejected Estimate v3: {reason}".
- **Inbox subject:** outcome and reply items stay open while their request is pending, never "Escalated". A superseded request now reads "Superseded by v4".
- **Reply:** `POST â€¦/review-requests/{rid}/replies` (new file `reviews/application/replies.py`) follows the spec's rules on who, when, Evidence, alternative and effect. It traces `reviews.review_request.replied` and gives the reviewer a "Reply on Estimate v3" item.
- **Supersede on submit:** `supersede_open_requests` (`reviews/application/supersede.py`) is called from submit for each superseded version.
  - Pending and challenged requests become `superseded`, each with its own trace event, and reviewers with nothing pending lose access.
  - If the latest reply named the new draft as the alternative, it creates the linked request on the new version, moves that version to `in_review` and notifies the reviewer.
- **New version:** `estimates.create_version` and `POST â€¦/estimate-versions/{vid}/new-version` (`estimates/application/versions.py`).
  - The base must be rejected or approved and no draft may exist; otherwise it returns 409.
  - It copies the lines with their Requirement links and carries the Assumptions, Risks and line edits through `store_version`.
  - The created event now records the base version and the reason.
- **Panel read** gains the author fields from the spec, plus `alternative_draft` (my addition: the draft the "Link as alternative" select offers). The Estimate view gains `can_create_version`.
- **Wiring:** two new actions for owners and collaborators, never sales representatives. Also three new 409 errors, the new trace events and the `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` ownership row.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_reviews_outcomes.py` covers every matrix row, no reminders after superseding, append-only replies and the migration down/up. I updated the two older tests that assumed 9.4 would supersede, plus five others whose exact payloads or flags changed.

**Web**
- New `review-outcomes.tsx` (the Review outcomes list) and `review-reply.tsx` (the Reply composer, Add Source, Link as alternative and the New version button). `EvidencePicker` is now exported from `finding-decisions.tsx`.
- **Author panel:** the reviewer actions are hidden. It shows "Escalated to {name}", the "All requested reviews approved. Baseline can be set." line with no button, and New version.
- **Reviewer panel:** it now shows "Alternative to the v{n} request" and the outcomes list. The outcomes list replaces the old "Decisions" history section in both panels.
- **Estimate tab:** New version sits next to the rejected pill, with the reviewer's reason.
- **Inbox:** outcome and reply items have the "Review" label. An outcome on an approved or rejected request opens a live panel; superseded and cancelled ones are greyed.
- **Live refresh and client:** the new events are added to the refresh lists, and `schema.d.ts` is regenerated.
- **Tests:** axe runs on every author panel state, and there are server-action tests for the two new calls.

**Deviations and risks**
- **Error code:** an unresolvable Evidence reference returns the existing `evidence_unresolvable` code, not the `evidence_unresolved` the spec names.
- **Evidence shape:** reply Evidence is stored and traced as `{kind, id, version}` rather than `{kind, id}`, because a Requirement or Source reference only resolves with its version.
- **Unspecified choices I made:**
  - A reviewer who is also the owner or sender gets no outcome item for their own decision.
  - No linked request is created when the reviewer authored the new version.
  - A linked request always targets the new Estimate Version, even if the original targeted an Assessment.
- **New version API:** it takes an optional reason, which the UI never sends. It has no `If-Match` check; only the 409 checks guard it.
- **Fix outside 9.4:** storing a version whose lines cover no Requirement would have inserted a null link row. It wasn't reachable before, but copied lines hit it, so I fixed it in `estimates/adapters/repository.py`.
- **Schema regeneration:** I generated `schema.d.ts` from a dumped `app.openapi()` file rather than a running uvicorn. The output should be identical.
- **New version side effects:** it queues an Assumption-proposal job and a Red Team Review, as every new version does, so those model jobs will run.
- **Not done:** I didn't rebase onto main (9.3 hasn't merged) or update the Obsidian demo note.</result>

## Intent

**Problem:** After 9.3 a reviewer can decide, but the author never hears about it and can't answer. A rejected version is a dead end. Submitting a newer version leaves the old requests pending: they keep reminders and access, and their approvals look valid.

**Approach:**
- Notify the owner and the requester on every decision.
- Give the author a view of the request, built from the mockup's Inbox review block. It has a **Review outcomes** list, a **Reply** with Evidence, **Link as alternative**, and on a rejected version **New version**.
- Hook `reviews.public.supersede_open_requests` into `estimates.submit_version`.

**Decisions (2026-10-26):**
- (1) Everything stays in this one spec.
- (2) **New version** copies the base version's lines, Assumptions and Risks.
- (3) Reply Evidence is a Requirement, a Source document, or a newly added Opportunity Source. Knowledge Source references are deferred.
- (4) **Link as alternative** records the new draft on the reply. When that draft is submitted, the supersede hook creates the linked request.

**Branch:** `task/story-9-4-review-outcomes` sits on the unmerged 9.3 branch (`4b9c2b3`). Rebase it onto main once 9.3 merges.

It never rules out `record.reviewer_id`. The panel's `is_author` does exclude the reviewer, and Story 9.3 allows the owner to be named reviewer. So through the API, an owner who is also the reviewer can reply to their own evidence or alternative request. The 403 description on the route ("never â€¦ the reviewer") promises a check that isn't there. No test covers this case.

- **"Superseded by vN" can name the wrong version.** `request_status` sets `superseded_by` from `ReviewableVersion.superseded_by_version`. That value is the Opportunity's *current (else latest)* version (`review_status._view`), not the version whose submit superseded the request. Once someone starts a new draft after v4 (for example via **New version**), a v3 request's Inbox label changes to "Superseded by v5". The submit-time version number is already in the `reviews.review_request.superseded` trace and should be stored or read from there.

- **A later reply silently drops the alternative.** `supersede_open_requests` only checks the request's *latest* reply for `alternative_version_id == new.id`. If the author links v4 and then sends a follow-up reply that adds only evidence (allowed, since the latest decision is still `alternative_requested`), submitting v4 creates no linked request. The reviewer is never asked to look at the alternative. It should check any reply on the request, or the latest reply that named an alternative.

- **A linked request always targets the Estimate Version.** `_link` hard-codes `target_kind=ESTIMATE_VERSION`, `target_id=new.id` and `target_version=new.version`, even when the original pending request was on an Assessment. An Assessment-targeted review (and its review type) is silently turned into an Estimate Version review. Nothing tests or documents this.

- **The alternative flow has no matching "start a draft" path.** An alternative must be "this Opportunity's draft â€¦ numbered above the one under review". But the only new author-facing way to make a draft, **New version** (`create_version` / `can_create_version`), only works from a `rejected` or `approved` base. While an alternative is requested, the version is still `submitted`/`in_review`, so the author can't copy it into a draft from the panel. Either allow **New version** from a version with an `alternative_requested` decision, or say how the author is expected to get a draft.

- **The UI can't send a reason for a new version.** The backend accepts and stores `NewVersionCreate.reason` (and traces it), but `createEstimateVersion` in `web/src/app/opportunities/actions.ts` always sends `body: {}`, and `NewVersionButton` has no reason field. # Epic 9 Context: Review, Challenge, Baseline and Decision Trace

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Put a qualified human between agent output and any committed figure. Named reviewers approve, reject or challenge a submitted Estimate Version (or specific Assessments). A Challenge reruns only the affected Assessments in a Workflow Run and produces a new Estimate Version with the delta, leaving the challenged version unchanged. Once every requested review is approved and nothing blocks it, the presales engineer sets the Baseline, and only a newer approved version can replace it. Anyone with access can trace any Estimate line or Assumption back to its Findings, Evidence and human decisions through an append-only Decision Trace whose completeness is tested. This closes the R1 loop from "submitted" to "baselined". Status: Story 9.8 is done (demo slice) and 9.1 is in review. Everything else is in the backlog and is built on the Epic 17 redesign.

# Epic 9 Context: Review, Challenge, Baseline and Decision Trace

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Put a qualified human between agent output and any committed figure. Named reviewers approve, reject or challenge a submitted Estimate Version (or specific Assessments). A Challenge reruns only the affected Assessments in a Workflow Run and produces a new Estimate Version with the delta, leaving the challenged version unchanged. Once every requested review is approved and nothing blocks it, the presales engineer sets the Baseline, and only a newer approved version can replace it. Anyone with access can trace any Estimate line or Assumption back to its Findings, Evidence and human decisions through an append-only Decision Trace whose completeness is tested. This closes the R1 loop from "submitted" to "baselined". Status: Story 9.8 is done (demo slice) and 9.1 is in review. Everything else is in the backlog and is built on the Epic 17 redesign.

    """The Opportunity as an authorization `Resource` (its owner and collaborators), for

    _, _, resource = await _load_readable(uow, actor, opportunity_id)

    user_id = actor.user_id

async def _view(uow: UnitOfWork, record: VersionRecord) -> ReviewableVersion:
    status = VersionStatus(record.status)
    replaced_by: int | None = None
    if status == VersionStatus.SUPERSEDED:
        current = await repo.current_version(uow, record.opportunity_id)
        replaced_by = (
            current.version
            if current is not None
            else await repo.latest_version_number(uow, record.opportunity_id)
        )
    return ReviewableVersion(
        id=record.id,
        opportunity_id=record.opportunity_id,
        version=record.version,
        status=status,
        row_version=record.row_version,
        created_by=record.created_by,
        submitted_at=record.submitted_at,
        superseded_by_version=replaced_by,
    )

_SEGMENT = r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*"
EVENT_TYPE_RE = re.compile(rf"^{_SEGMENT}\.{_SEGMENT}\.{_SEGMENT}$")
# Past tense check on the verb's last word: regular verbs end in "ed"; list irregular
# past participles here when an event needs one. This is a heuristic, not a guarantee:
# non-past words that end in "ed" (need, seed) also pass, so reviewers still check names.
_IRREGULAR_PAST_TENSE = frozenset(
    {"built", "done", "lost", "made", "overridden", "run", "sent", "split", "won"}
)
# State events: names that report a state entered rather than a past-tense verb. Kept to the
# few the architecture names verbatim (Story 5.5: AD-7's `workflows.run.waiting_for_human`).
_STATE_EVENTS = frozenset({"workflows.run.waiting_for_human"})


def is_valid_event_type(name: str) -> bool:
    """Shape check plus the past-tense heuristic above (not a grammatical guarantee), or one
    of the allow-listed state events."""
    if not EVENT_TYPE_RE.match(name):
        return False
    if name in _STATE_EVENTS:
        return True
    last_word = name.rsplit(".", 1)[1].rsplit("_", 1)[-1]
    return last_word.endswith("ed") or last_word in _IRREGULAR_PAST_TENSE

Paths below are relative to `D:\Projects\Office\pre-sales-agent-95\web\src\`. I used Grep and Read because graft's MCP index points at the main checkout.

**1. Dialog, ReasonInput, InlineAlert, Button**
- **Dialog** is `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, built on base-ui. It exports `Dialog` (`open`/`onOpenChange`), `DialogTrigger`, `DialogContent` (`showCloseButton`, default true, :42), `DialogHeader`, `DialogFooter` (:93, grey footer band), `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription` and `DialogClose`.

- **Template to copy:** `components/opportunities/request-review-dialog.tsx:206-424` (Story 9.1, written to the Challenge-dialog conventions). It already has:
  - an outline trigger and `<form noValidate>` inside `DialogContent showCloseButton={false}` (:298);
  - an uppercase `text-eyebrow` group heading (:350-353);
  - `aria-pressed` toggle cards (:357-381): `border-primary bg-primary-tint` when ticked, and an 18px box filled `bg-primary` with a `CheckIcon`;
  - helper text (:384), an inline `role="alert"` problem line (:406), and `DialogClose` Cancel plus a submit button (:415-420).
- **Confirm dialogs with a reason:**
  - Cancel request: `review-requests-card.tsx:123-186` (Textarea plus reason).
  - Override confirm: `finding-decisions.tsx:544-564`.
  - Cancel run: `specialist-assessments.tsx:962-1003`.
- **ReasonInput** is `components/opportunities/reason-input.tsx:14`. Props: `label, value, onChange, error, disabled, inputRef?, max?` (default `REASON_MAX`). It renders 2 rows with a code-point counter and has **no placeholder prop**, so the placeholder needs adding, or use `ui/textarea`.
- **InlineAlert** is `components/ui/inline-alert.tsx:22`. Props: `lead, onReload, reloading, reloadRef, onViewDiff, viewDiffLabel, diffExpanded`. It is meant for 412s.
- **Button** is `components/ui/button.tsx:5-47`.
  - Variants: `default` (primary, 38px), `outline`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `destructive`, `link`.
  - Sizes: `default`, `xs`, `sm`, `lg`, plus the `icon*` sizes.

**2. `review-panel.tsx`**
- **Challenge button:** :366-374. It is `aria-disabled="true"` and described by `challengeHintId`, with the hint at :380-382 (`CHALLENGE_LATER`, `lib/reviews.ts:173`). The tests that assert it are `review-panel.test.tsx:87-94`.
- `ReasonedDecision` deliberately leaves out `challenged` (`lib/reviews.ts:158-164`).
- **Posting:** `decide()` at :487-514 calls `decideReviewRequest`.
  - Action: `app/opportunities/actions.ts:3491`, with `DecideInput`/`DecideResult` at :3454-3473. It sends `If-Match` set to the request's `row_version`.
  - `DECISION_VALUES` (:3446-3452) also leaves out `challenged`, so it must be added or a separate challenge action written.
  - Error mapping: `problemOf` at :261. A 412 shows an InlineAlert at :600-608.
- **Reload and announce:** on success it calls `announce(decisionAnnouncement(...))` (useAnnounce from `components/shell/live-region.tsx:76`), then `onDecided`. `ReviewPanelLoader` (:629) patches the panel with `afterDecision` (:435) and re-reads through `loadReviewPanel` (`actions.ts:3440`) on Reload and when `useReviewEvents` fires (:692).
- The panel is mounted in three places:
  - Inbox: `inbox-view.tsx:194`
  - Estimate inspector: `estimate-grid.tsx:1213`
  - Full page: `app/opportunities/[id]/estimate/reviews/[rid]/page.tsx:39`

**3. Assessments tab**
- **Main file:** `components/opportunities/specialist-assessments.tsx`.
  - `SpecialistAssessmentsSection`: :1228
  - `FindingsTable`: :232-368. Each row is a single `<button data-finding-row data-finding-id={key}>` and there are **no row actions**.
  - `AssessmentCard`: :472-519 (only Show effort).

  - Each specialist `AssessmentFinding` has a UUID `id` and a `position` (`lib/api/schema.d.ts:2857`). The parent `AssessmentView` has `id`, `agent`, `version` and `run_id` (:2984).

- **Detail branching:** `inbox-view.tsx:173-212`. Only `subject_type === REVIEW_SUBJECT` (`"reviews.review_request"`, `lib/inbox.ts:33`) with an `opportunity_id` renders `ReviewPanelLoader`. Everything else gets `DetailBody` (:148).

**6. Activity and the event stream**
- The right pane's **Activity tab is a placeholder** that only shows "No activity yet." (`components/shell/right-pane.tsx:106-114`).

Paths below are relative to `D:\Projects\Office\pre-sales-agent-95\backend`.

### 1. reviews module after 9.3
- **Files:** `app/modules/reviews/{domain/requests.py, domain/decisions.py, application/{decisions,requests,public,models,reminders}.py, adapters/{models,repository}.py, api/routes.py}`.
- **`decide` flow** (`application/decisions.py:206`): `opportunities.readable_resource` â†’ `identity.authorize(REVIEW_REQUEST_DECIDE)` (215-216) â†’ `estimates.lock_for_review` (217) â†’ `repo.get(..., for_update=True)` with a 404 check (218-220) â†’ reviewer and role check (221) â†’ superseded check giving 409 (223-225) â†’ self-approval check (226) â†’ reason (229) â†’ must be pending (230) â†’ `_check_if_match` (232).
- **Writes:** `repo.insert_decision` (236), then `repo.set_status`, `reassign` or `bump`, all with `expected_row_version` (246-262). Then version roll-up (264-272), reviewer access grant/revoke (273-284), `trace.append(ReviewsReviewDecisionRecorded)` (285-302) and `notify_reviewer` (303-315).
- **Helpers to reuse:**
  - `decisions.py`: `_check_if_match`/`_stale` (135-149, the "Changed by {name}" message), `_is_reviewer`, `_holds_role`, `_is_author` (123-132).
  - `requests.py`: `superseded_detail` (125), `opportunity_title` (443), `notify_reviewer` (447), `target_labels` (507), `request_views` (552), `request_status` (688), `ROLE_FOR_TYPE` (103), `MAX_ROW_VERSION` (102).
  - `adapters/repository.py`: `get(for_update)` (95), `set_status` (188), `insert_decision` (312), `latest_decisions` (357), `has_pending_for_reviewer` (161).
- **State machine** (`domain/requests.py:116-132`): `pending â†’ challenged` is allowed. `challenged â†’ pending` is not; `challenged` can only become `superseded`. `tests/test_reviews_requests.py:48-57` (`ALLOWED`) lists every pair and must change if you add a move.
- **Request status is stored, not derived.** `status_after()` (`domain/decisions.py:36-48`) maps `CHALLENGED â†’ RequestStatus.CHALLENGED`, and `set_status` writes it on the request row.
- **Where `challenged` is blocked or listed today:**
  - `RECORDABLE` leaves it out (`domain/decisions.py:33`), and `_clean_reason` returns a 422 "Challenge arrives with Story 9.5." (`decisions.py:106, 153-154`). The test `test_a_challenge_is_not_recorded_yet` (`tests/test_reviews_decisions.py:527`) expects that.
  - DB checks: request status (`adapters/models.py:41`), decision (`:78`).
  - Trace `Literal` (`app/platform/trace/catalogue.py:1384`).
  - `OPEN_STATUSES` (`domain/requests.py:135`, a baseline blocker).
- **Gotcha:** once a request leaves `pending`, `decide` calls `revoke_reviewer_access` (278-284). A challenger with no other pending request loses read access to the Opportunity, so their Inbox item and any later decline/confirm notice would point at something they can no longer open.

### 2. Migrations
- **Latest:** `migrations/versions/20261026_0049_reviews_review_decisions.py`, revision `"0049_reviews_review_decisions"`, down `"0048_notifications"`. The next file would be `20261026_0050_...` with `down_revision = "0049_reviews_review_decisions"`.
- **Grants:** append-only tables use `GRANT SELECT, INSERT` plus `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` (0049 lines 77-78). Mutable ones use `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (`0047...:100`, `0048...:167`).
- **Check constraints:** explicit `ck_<table>_<name>` in `op.create_table`. To change one, use `drop_constraint`, then `create_check_constraint` (0049:80-85).
- **`migrations/env.py:14-31`:** imports every `app.modules.*.adapters.models`; `reviews` is already there (line 24).
- **Kind check:** `notifications_notifications.kind` is a DB check (`app/modules/notifications/adapters/models.py:12-15, 27`; migration `0048:154`). New kinds need a migration.

### 3. workflows
- **`start_run`:** `app/modules/workflows/application/assessment_runs.py:288`. Signature: `async def start_run(uow, actor: Principal, opportunity_id: UUID) -> AssessmentRun`.
  - No `run_type`, `trigger_ref` or idempotency key, anywhere under `app` or `migrations`.
  - It authorizes `ASSESSMENT_START`, locks runs, and returns 409 `AssessmentInProgressError` if any run is active. It does not return the existing run.
  - `enqueue_run` (`runs.py:222`, exposed at `public.py:72`) runs as the system and coalesces, returning the active run's id. Duplicates are detected per Opportunity only.
  - There is no `platform_idempotency` table, although the architecture spine (`_bmad-output/.../ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:305-306`) requires one.
- **What a run holds:** `workflows_runs` (`adapters/models.py:42-66`) has only id, opportunity_id, status, plan_version and timestamps. Its status check covers status only; there is no `run_type` column.
- **Fixed plan:** `queue_run` (`runs.py:184`) always plans the 3 specialists plus `critic_agent` after them. Agent checks: `workflows/adapters/models.py:31`, `TaskAgent` (`domain/runs.py:25-32`).
- **Worker:** `_execute` (`runs.py:779`) gives the installed graph runner the run's planned tasks (`plan_of`). There is no dispatch on run type, so a "challenge" run would just run as a normal assessment. It wouldn't crash, but nothing would make it challenge-specific.
- **Red Team is a separate job:** it runs from `assessments_red_team_runs` via `assessments.enqueue_review` (`assessments/application/public.py:84`), not as a workflows task.
- **Activity tab:** the frontend shows a placeholder, "No activity yet." (`web/src/components/shell/right-pane.tsx:15,113`). The backend serves runs through `GET /opportunities/{id}/assessments` (latest run only, `workflows/api/routes.py:81`) and the SSE `GET /opportunities/{id}/events` (`routes.py:198`). There is no list-runs endpoint.

### 4. assessments
- **`AssessmentRow`** (`assessments_assessments`, `adapters/models.py:280-327`): id, opportunity_id, `agent` (checked against engineering/pm/security only, `:276`), version, run_id, config_version_id, status (`current`/`superseded`), recommendation and confidence.

- **Finding:** `AssessmentFindingRow` (`assessments_assessment_findings`, `:330-358`) is a real insert-only row with its own UUID, tied to one Assessment row. So `{kind: finding, id, version}` would point at an immutable row.

  - Requirements it cites: `assessments_assessment_finding_requirements` (`:361`), stored as (requirement_id, requirement_version).
  - **No Integration Type or catalogue link.** Integration Types are tagged per Requirement in `intake_requirement_integration_types` (`intake/adapters/models.py:205-226`, read by `requirements_repository.integration_type_ids` at `:1136`).

- **Critic and Red Team** are not Assessments. They live in `assessments_reviews` with `kind IN ('red_team','critic')` (`adapters/models.py:58-90`), and their Findings are in `assessments_findings` (`:108`). The Critic's citations of specialist Findings are in `assessments_finding_targets` (`:252`).
- **No Research agent** exists as an Assessment agent.
- **Public reads** (`assessments/application/public.py`):
  - `assessment_at(uow, assessment_id, version)` (`assessments.py:163`)
  - `agent_assessments(uow, opp)` (current ones, `:157`)
  - `current_finding_snapshots`, `run_finding_snapshots`, `finding_titles` (`assessment.py:334-381`)
  - `get_critic`, `get_red_team`, `CRITIC_AGENT`, `AGENTS`
  - The repo's `findings_of` and `requirement_links_for` (`assessment_repository.py:262,307`) are not public.

### 5. identity
- **Actions:** `Action` StrEnum in `app/modules/identity/actions.py:22`, three-segment names enforced by the regex at :19 (`reviews.challenge.raise` fits). Each gets a category in `ACTION_CATEGORIES` (:118-195); `tests/test_tool_gateway.py:144` fails if one is missing. Pattern to copy: `REVIEW_REQUEST_DECIDE` (:81).
- **Policy** (`app/modules/identity/domain/policy.py`):
  - `RELATION_EXCLUDED_ROLES` (78-103) excludes sales reps.
  - `OWNER_GRANTS` (106-140), `MEMBER_GRANTS` (141-171).
  - `REVIEWER_GRANTS = {OPPORTUNITY_READ, REVIEW_REQUEST_DECIDE}` (172-174).
  - `is_allowed` (201-232).

### 6. notifications
- **`notify`:** `notify(uow, *, recipient_id, kind, opportunity_id, subject_type, subject_id, subject_version, summary, dedupe_key) -> bool` (`app/modules/notifications/application/notify.py:29`).
- **Kinds:** `NotificationKind` (`domain/notifications.py:23-28`) has review_requested, review_reminder, review_cancelled, run_waiting, conflict_escalated. `InboxGroup.CHALLENGES` exists but no kind maps to it in `KIND_GROUP` (:50-56).
- **Live status** (`application/inbox.py:77-117`): an if-chain per `subject_type` (`REVIEW_SUBJECT`, `DECISION_SUBJECT`, `CONFLICT_SUBJECT` at :36-38), each lazily importing the owning module's public status read.
- **Adding a challenge subject needs:** new kinds plus `KIND_GROUP` entries, a migration for the kind check, a `CHALLENGE_SUBJECT` branch calling something like `reviews.challenge_status`, and labels. The frontend `kindLabel` (`web/src/lib/inbox*.ts`) also needs updating.

- **Current version:** `current_reviewable_version(uow, opp)` (`app/modules/estimates/application/review_status.py:82`) returns the draft, otherwise the latest submitted, in_review, approved or rejected version. `reviewable_version(uow, version_id)` is at :76.

"""Authorization policy (AD-15): which permissions, and which relations to a resource, grant

Three kinds of grant, any of which allows an action:

Because the two cards are stacked, their left edges and label columns will visibly not line up, which defeats the "same visual language" goal.

  - Review Request sent: the reviewer gets an item.

![The review panel for a reviewer, with both action rows](https://github.com/shanilmelder/pre-sales-agent/blob/task/story-9-3-review-decisions/docs/pr-assets/story-9-3-review-decisions.png?raw=true)

### What changes
- **Review Decisions:** a new append-only `reviews_review_decisions` table. `psa_app` gets SELECT and INSERT only.
  - A reviewer can approve, reject, request evidence, request an alternative or escalate. Every decision except Approve needs a reason.
  - The request's status comes from its latest decision.

  - A stale `If-Match` is 412. Deciding on a request that isn't pending is 409.
  - When every request for a version is approved, the version becomes `approved`. A rejection makes it `rejected`.
  - An escalation reassigns the request and moves reviewer access. The new reviewer gets an Inbox item.

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Give the presales engineer one standard Estimate whose numbers are always calculated by the platform, never by a model. Every open Gap, Unknown or Finding becomes an explicit Condition, Contingency or Risk with a named accepting person, so nothing is quietly assumed away. One live Submission Blockers gate counts down to zero before an Estimate Version can be submitted, and the Overview shows where the submission stands. ## Overview

This document breaks the whole Pre Sales Agent Framework into epics and stories for all four Releases (R1â€“R4), covering FR-1..FR-67. It draws on the PRD, the architecture spine (AD-1 to AD-33), the UX design contract (DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md), and the original orchestration engine specification, whose acceptance criteria are reused where they map. **Where the PRD and the architecture spine disagree, the spine wins.** See the spine's "PRD Deviations" section: local Ollama models, a single VPS with queued runs, sops-encrypted secrets, OpenTelemetry to a local collector instead of LangSmith, and SSE only.

## Requirements Inventory
### Release 1: Estimation core
### Epic 1: Secure workspace on the production server
The team signs in with Auth0, creates and shares Opportunities, and works inside the app shell. The platform runs on the production VPS from day one, with CI/CD, backups and alerts. Delivers the project scaffold and the shared platform layer (Unit of Work, authorization, trace, design tokens).

<result>Story 8.9 is implemented in `D:/Projects/Office/pre-sales-agent-89` (branch `task/story-8-9-overview-recomposition`), with nothing committed. The pipeline's Blocked states now come only from the API's blockers view, and lint, typecheck, the full test suite (2137 tests, axe included) and the build all pass.

**What changed**
- **`web/src/lib/overview.ts`**:
  - The pipeline now has 8 steps, each with its tab, and four states: Complete, In progress, Blocked and Pending.
  - The old browser rules that decided Blocked are gone, and `pipelineSteps` now takes the blockers view as an input.
  - Review and Baseline follows the spec's states and is never Complete.
  - New footer labels ("2 of 8 steps complete", "3 steps blocked").
  - The Estimate KPI label now reads "Estimate Â· v3 draft" or "Estimate Â· v3 submitted".
- **`overview-pipeline.tsx` (new, client)**:
  - The pipeline card reads the live view from the workspace provider, falling back to the server's read.
  - Each step title links to its tab, and each pill has an icon plus text.
  - Screen readers hear the footer as "2 of 8 steps complete Â· 3 steps blocked".
  - A small client pill on the Conflicts KPI shows "Blocks submit" when there are `conflict` blockers.
- **`overview-summary.tsx`**: uses the new pipeline and KPI pill, and Agent run tasks are now a 3-column grid.
- **`overview-live-refresh.tsx` (new)**:
  - Calls `router.refresh()` 300 ms after the last event, and ignores each hook's first connect callback.
  - It listens to progress, Gaps, Conflicts, blocker, Source and Review events.
  - It replaces `GapsLiveRefresh` in `app/opportunities/[id]/overview.tsx`. The old component stays in the codebase because it has its own test, but nothing on the Overview uses it now.
- **Tests**:
  - `overview.test.ts` has a test for every matrix row plus all the Review and Baseline states.
  - The new `overview-summary.test.tsx` checks axe, the pill and link on every step, that nothing is `aria-disabled`, a blocker event flipping the Conflicts step live, and the debounced refresh.
  - I also updated the existing Overview expectations in `pages.test.tsx` to the 8 steps and new states.
- **Spec**: I ticked the tasks and added Implementation Notes. The frozen section is untouched.

**Choices the spec left open, worth a look**
- **Open items with no blockers**: if the view has no items for a step, the step is Complete once it has run, even when the tab's own read still shows open items. That is what makes "Live clear" turn Complete on the same frame as the card, while the read is still stale. In that case the sub-line says "No Gaps block submission" or "No Conflicts block submission" rather than "No open â€¦".
- **"Needs a decision" pill**: the Conflicts KPI still shows "Needs a decision" (now in amber instead of red) when Conflicts are open but none of them block.
- **A failed tab read can still be Blocked**: if the blockers say "blocked" for a step whose own read failed (Gaps, Estimate or Conflicts), the step still shows Blocked. Its sub-line falls back to the count from the blockers, for example "3 open".

**Risks and gaps**
- The mockup file (`new-mockups/â€¦standalone.html`) isn't in this worktree or the main checkout, so I built the visuals from the spec and the existing Overview card. I didn't compare pixels or take screenshots.
- I didn't run it in a browser; everything was verified with tests and the build.

## Intent

**Problem:** The Overview (redesigned earlier) has a 7-step pipeline that decides "Blocked" with its own browser rules. It uses "Not started" and "Unknown" states, its steps don't link anywhere, and it only re-renders on navigation. So it can disagree with the Submission blockers check (AD-27) and go stale.

**Approach:** Recompose the Overview to the new mockup (`new-mockups/â€¦standalone.html`, Overview section). The pipeline gets 8 steps and the states Complete, In progress, Blocked and Pending. Every Blocked state comes from the API's blockers view, which is the same view the card, badge and header read. Each step links to its tab, and the Overview refreshes live over SSE. This is web-only: no backend, API or migration change.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `web/src/lib/overview.ts` -- 8 steps, blocker-driven Blocked, Review and Baseline, pending states, `tab` per step, footer labels -- AD-27 single rule
- [x] `web/src/components/opportunities/overview-pipeline.tsx` (new, client) -- the mockup card reading `useSubmission()` with a fallback; step title links -- UX-DR29
- [x] `web/src/components/opportunities/overview-summary.tsx` -- use the new pipeline;… (+879 chars)
