Its promise that "nothing the checks read changes alongside" depends on those commands holding the same lock.
- **Existing test evidence:** `backend/tests/test_estimates_baseline.py` has two two-engine race tests:
  - `test_a_rejection_and_the_baseline_serialise_on_the_lock` (`reviews.decide` against `set_baseline`)
  - `test_the_baseline_first_holds_off_a_new_version` (`set_baseline` against `create_version`)

  `tests/test_estimates_submit.py` has `test_accept_and_submit_serialise_on_the_lock` (`accept_assumption` against `submit_version`). I searched the tests for `opportunity_lock|pg_locks|advisory`: the only hits are `test_estimates_baseline.py` (the key-arithmetic unit test) and `test_tool_gateway_unauthorized.py`, which isn't related. No test files under `tests/test_gaps*` or `tests/test_assessments_findings*` use `asyncio.Event` or `create_task`, so none of them run a concurrent case.
- **Missing verification:** A two-engine test where a Gap reopen (or a Finding override's un-resolve) holds the shared lock uncommitted. It should assert that `set_baseline` blocks, then returns 409 `baseline_blocked` listing `gap` (or `finding`).
- **Demonstration:** Suppose `gap_commands._authorized` or `findings._load` went back to a module-private key, or dropped the lock. A Gap reopened at the same moment as `set_baseline` could commit after the gate read an empty `to_baseline`, and the Baseline would be written over an open Gap. The two existing race tests only exercise `reviews.decide` and `create_version`, so neither would fail.
- **Consequence:** The spec's main serialisation promise (Gaps, Findings and conversion against the Baseline) holds only through inspection. No test pins it.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add `test_a_gap_reopen_and_the_baseline_serialise_on_the_lock` to `test_estimates_baseline.py`, modelled on the existing rejection race test.

### Keeping an earlier version selected on reload (`pinned`) in the Estimate tab is untested

  - The existing `loadEstimate` assertions (`toHaveBeenCalledWith(OPP_ID)` at lines 546 and 607) cover current-version views only.
- **Missing verification:** With `is_current: false` (for example `?version=2`), trigger `reloadReviews` (a review frame, or Set Baseline success with `setEstimateBaseline` mocked to `ok`). Assert that `loadEstimate` was called with `(OPP_ID, 2)`.

- **Consequence:** A read-only historical view can silently jump to the current version after a live update.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add one case to the "EstimateSection, the Baseline (Story 9.7)" describe block that confirms Set Baseline on an earlier version and asserts the `loadEstimate(OPP_ID, n)` call.

- **The shared lock creates a new lock-order cycle with the Red Team lock, which can deadlock.**

# Goods-to-person picking ports: design and operation guide

Synthetic product documentation for demos.

## Throughput

A conveyor port delivers 150 to 180 bins per hour per operator at steady state; a carousel
port reaches 300. Peak design should use the busiest hour of the busiest week plus 20 %
headroom. For a new sales channel with no history, model a low and a high case and carry the
difference as a contingency.

## Operator sign-on

Operators sign on at each port with a badge or with single sign-on through the operator
portal. Supported identity providers: Microsoft Entra ID and Okta (OIDC). The customer must
choose the provider and supply a test tenant; the choice changes the configuration work
(Entra ID about 16 hours, Okta about 20 hours).

## Ergonomics and safety

Port work surfaces are height-adjustable between 850 and 1,100 mm. Light curtains stop bin
movement when an operator reaches into the port opening.

## Acceptance testing

Site acceptance testing needs a set of representative test orders prepared by the customer
(typically 500 to 1,000 orders covering every order profile) and two to four trained
super-users per shift.

## Intent

**Problem:** After 9.3 and 9.4 an Estimate Version can be `approved`, but nothing turns it into the committed figure. The review panel says "Baseline can be set." and offers no action. The Overview pipeline is stuck on "Approved, Baseline not set yet". Every module also takes its own advisory lock, so a rejection can race a Baseline.

**Approach:** Add `estimates_baselines` and the human-only `estimates.set_baseline` command behind one shared per-Opportunity lock (`platform.locks.opportunity_lock`), and make the Baseline gate and the command read the same blocker check. Then surface it as the **new mockup** draws it: the Set Baseline confirm dialog, the Baseline marker, the lifecycle stepper reaching Baseline, and the "Blockers to Baseline" gate going to "0 blockers to Baseline".

**Mockup wins (user, 2026-10-26: "follow the new mockups").** Where the epic and the mockup differ, use the mockup:
- Use the mockup's dialog warning copy.
- Use the mockup's approver rows.
- Use the mockup's four-step lifecycle.
- Add the anchor icon to the marker, because DESIGN.md:369 requires it.

# Automated packing line guide (auto-bagger and carton erector)

Synthetic product documentation for demos.

## Carton range

The carton erector handles 6 to 12 carton sizes from 200 x 150 x 100 mm to 600 x 400 x 400 mm.
The auto-bagger handles soft and flat goods up to 450 x 350 mm. The customer fixes the final
carton range; each additional size adds a format change kit and about 6 hours of
configuration and test. The range must be frozen before factory acceptance testing.

## Product data

Right-size packing depends on accurate SKU dimensions and weights. With unreliable item
data, expect 3 to 8 % of orders to be rejected to manual packing until data is cleaned.

## Throughput

One erector and bagger pair packs up to 900 orders per hour. Allow 15 % for jams and
changeovers in peak planning.

## Returns

Returns processing (unpack, grade, re-bin) is a separate work cell. Including it in the
first phase adds about 3 weeks of installation and 80 engineering hours.

# Parcel sortation and carrier integration guide

Synthetic product documentation for demos.

## Sorter capacity

A tilt-tray or cross-belt sorter for e-commerce parcels runs 3,000 to 6,000 items per hour.
Plan one chute per carrier service per dispatch wave, plus reject and no-read chutes.

## Carrier integration

Each parcel carrier needs label generation, manifest upload and tracking events. Typical
effort per carrier: 40 to 60 engineering hours using the carrier REST API, 80 hours where
only EDI is offered. If the carrier tender is still open at proposal stage, price a named
allowance per carrier rather than a fixed scope.

## Label print and apply

Print-and-apply units need 400 mm of straight conveyor and a carrier-certified printer
(203 or 300 dpi). Carrier label certification takes 2 to 4 weeks per carrier.

## Network

Sorter PLCs and scanners sit on the automation VLAN. Shared VLANs with office traffic are not
supported for scanner traffic because of latency limits (under 50 ms).

1. **Deadlock (lock order):** `opportunity_lock` is now taken before the module lock in:
   - `review.py` `enqueue_review`, `accept_red_team_review` and `_start`;
   - `critic.py` `accept_critic_review`;

   - `stamp` is called only from the Red Team and Critic accept paths, both now fixed.
   - `lock_agent` never reaches the shared lock.
   - The workflows run lock already takes the shared lock first.
   - The conflicts and intake paths either take the shared lock first or never take it after their own lock.

   - Backend: `baseline_version` is now on `VersionGate` and on the submission-blockers view.

4. **Switcher:** `switcherVersions(versions, selected)` adds the selected version as its own segment when it isn't one already, so it shows as pressed. `VersionStatePill`'s signature is wrapped.
5. **`estimate-grid.tsx`:** the four calls are now plain `loadEstimate(opportunityId, pinned)`. Existing assertions changed from `(OPP_ID)` to `(OPP_ID, null)` in `estimate-grid.test.tsx` and `assumption-inspector.test.tsx`.
6. **`?version=` too large:** the query now has `le=2**31 - 1`, and a test asserts 422 for 2^31.
7. **New backend tests:**
   - A two-engine race where a Gap reopen holds the lock uncommitted; `set_baseline` waits, then gets 409 `baseline_blocked` listing `gap`. The test patches the inserted Gap's trigger, because the shared fixture's empty trigger fails the Gap read model.
   - A newer `in_review` version with a Baseline in place gets `baseline_not_newer`.
   - Asserts on `baseline_version`.
8. **New web tests:**
   - Set Baseline on a non-current v2 calls `loadEstimate(OPP_ID, 2)`.
   - An older version chosen from All versions gets its own pressed segment.
   - The replaced, superseded and rejected reasons.
   - The new `switcherVersions` cases.

"""Refuse a `document.xml` that would inflate past this (a zip bomb)."""
_W = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main}"
_P, _T, _TAB, _BR, _CR = f"{_W}p", f"{_W}t", f"{_W}tab", f"{_W}br", f"{_W}cr"
_FALLBACK = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006}Fallback"
_DECLARATIONS = (b"<!DOCTYPE", b"<!ENTITY")


def _paragraphs(element: ET.Element) -> list[ET.Element]:
    """Every `w:p` in document order, outside `mc:Fallback` subtrees."""
    found: list[ET.Element] = []

    def walk(node: ET.Element) -> None:
        for child in node:
            if child.tag == _FALLBACK:
                continue
            if child.tag == _P:
                found.append(child)
            walk(child)

    walk(element)
    return found

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Close the loop between estimating and delivery. Delivery managers record Actuals (hours, duration, cost) against each Baseline Estimate line with a variance cause, by hand or by file import. The Head of Delivery sees in Reports where estimates are consistently wrong and drills from an overrun to the Assumption that failed and its decision chain. The epic also records each Opportunity's outcome (won/lost), which fixes its retention date, and adds the controlled, privileged purge job that is the only thing allowed to delete Opportunity data once retention ends. It finishes with the Pipeline report. The result is a reliable estimate-vs-delivery history that later calibration depends on, while meeting deletion duties without weakening the append-only audit trail.

#!/bin/sh
# Creates the least-privileged login role the application connects as (`psa_app`).
#
# Run by the postgres image's entrypoint from /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d on first start of
# an empty data volume only. Existing volumes need `docker compose down -v` once.
# CI runs this script directly against its Postgres service (PGHOST/PGPASSWORD set).
#
# Table privileges are granted by Alembic migrations, which run as the owner role.
# Requires: POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_DB, PSA_APP_DB_PASSWORD.

set -e

if [ -z "${PSA_APP_DB_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    echo "10-app-role.sh: PSA_APP_DB_PASSWORD must be set" >&2
    exit 1
fi

psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
    --username "$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname "$POSTGRES_DB" \
    -v app_password="$PSA_APP_DB_PASSWORD" -v db_name="$POSTGRES_DB" <<'EOSQL'
SELECT format('CREATE ROLE psa_app LOGIN PASSWORD %L', :'app_password')
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'psa_app')
\gexec
SELECT format('ALTER ROLE psa_app WITH LOGIN PASSWORD %L', :'app_password')
\gexec
GRANT CONNECT, TEMPORARY ON DATABASE :"db_name" TO psa_app;
EOSQL

"""The action catalogue (AD-15): every authorizable action, in one place.

Names follow `<module>.<entity>.<verb>` and match the command that performs them. The
Agent Registry reuses these names later. Auth0 RBAC permissions use the same names: a token
whose `permissions` claim holds an action's value is granted that action.

Story 7.4: every action has exactly one permission category (`ACTION_CATEGORIES`): `read`,
`write`, `delete`, `send` or `approve`. An Agent may be granted only `read` actions that are
also ToolGateway tools (the registry rejects anything else with
`registry_permission_forbidden_for_agents`).
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping
from enum import StrEnum
from types import MappingProxyType

_SEGMENT = r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*"
ACTION_NAME_RE = re.compile(rf"^{_SEGMENT}\.{_SEGMENT}\.{_SEGMENT}$")


class Action(StrEnum):

    settings: Settings = request.app.state.settings
    incoming = MultipartFile(

        field="file",
        max_body=intake.max_body_bytes(settings.upload_max_bytes),
    )

        uow,
        actor,
        incoming,
        store=BlobStore(settings.storage_dir),
        max_bytes=settings.upload_max_bytes,
        content_length=_content_length(request),

<result>Story 10.6 is implemented in the `pre-sales-agent-106` worktree and all the spec's verification checks pass. Nothing is committed yet. I also ticked the task checkboxes and added implementation notes in the spec, outside its frozen section.

**Verification**
- **Targeted backend tests:** `test_purge`, `test_retention_api`, `test_trace` and `test_db_roles` pass on `psa_test106`, along with the auth, seed, architecture, trace-catalogue, tool-gateway, jobs, worker and storage tests.
- **Full backend suite:** 2,946 passed, 1 skipped. `test_evals.py` was excluded because it resets the separate eval database.
- **Static checks:** `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy app` and `lint-imports` (24 contracts) are clean.
- **Migration:** 0058 upgrades, downgrades and re-upgrades cleanly, and `alembic check` shows no drift.
- **Web:** `npm run typecheck` and `npx eslint src` are clean. Vitest passes for `src/app/admin`, `src/components/admin`, `src/lib` and `src/test` (748 tests, axe included).

**What was built**
- **Database role and schedule:** migration `20261028_0058_purge_role.py` creates `psa_purge`. It can log in only if `PSA_PURGE_DB_PASSWORD` is set when the migration runs. The migration grants exactly the access the spec lists, including current and future checkpoint tables. It also adds the daily `platform.purge` schedule and an index for listing recent purges. `ops/postgres/init/20-purge-role.sh` creates the role on a fresh volume.
- **Configuration:** `PSA_PURGE_DATABASE_URL` is set only on the worker in both compose files and is documented in `.env.example`. If it is unset or blank, the job logs `purge.not_configured` and deletes nothing.
- **The purge job** (`backend/app/platform/purge/`):
  - Each due Opportunity is purged in its own transaction, and the `platform.purge.completed` event is written in that same transaction.
  - File reference counts are decremented; a file left with no references is deleted from disk only after the commit.
  - If any Opportunity fails, the others still run and the job raises so it retries with backoff.
  - On the last attempt it first queues a `purge_failed` alert email containing only counts and UUIDs.
- **Per-module steps:** each of the 11 modules has its own `adapters/purge.py`, registered by its `application/purge.py`. Only the worker loads these; an import-linter contract keeps them and the job out of the API process.
- **Due list:** opportunities supplies it using the existing domain rule (`retention_until`), not SQL date maths.
- **Alerts:** the alert-email job payload is now a union of the denial alert and the new purge alert, keyed on `kind`. It is stored flat, so alert jobs already in the queue still load.
- **Retention API:** `GET /api/v1/admin/retention`, read only, gated by the new `platform.retention.read` permission. I added that permission to the action catalogue, `seed_auth0.py`, the README and the web test permissions.
- **Web:** a new Admin â†’ Retention tab with two tables (Due for purge, Recent purges), empty states and the required footnote. It has no delete control. It also adds the trace label for the purge event and the regenerated API types.
- **Runbook:** `ops/runbooks/restore.md` covers the 35-day backup age-out and the steps to run the purge after a restore, before users return.

**Things that differ from what you might assume**
- **API location:** the retention endpoint lives in the `opportunities` module. The existing import rules stop the registry module from importing other modules and stop `platform` from importing `identity`, so neither could host it.
- **Platform rows:** the job deletes the platform's own rows itself (trace, model and tool calls, jobs), matched by Opportunity or by its workflow runs. Checkpoint threads are deleted in the workflows step.
- **File rows:** the purge role can decrement counts but not delete rows, so `platform_files` rows stay at a count of zero. A later upload of the same file counts up from there.
- **Downgrade:** rolling back migration 0058 removes the role's grants in that database but leaves the `psa_purge` role itself, because roles are shared across the whole Postgres server.
- **Test-file edits:** I edited two existing test files. `test_authorize.py`'s module list now includes `platform`, which the required name `platform.retention.read` needs. `test_tool_gateway_unauthorized.py` now wraps alerts in the new payload type.

**Risks**
- **File race:** there is a small window where an upload of identical bytes could lose its file on disk. That happens if the upload finds the file already present just before the purge deletes it, and only adds its reference afterwards. Locking the file row while deleting narrows the window but does not close it.
- **Test isolation:** the tests share one database and run a purge across all of it, so they leave nothing due behind. One test leaves a won Opportunity whose retention date is 1 Jan 2027. It is harmless because the tests pin today's date, but a future test that uses the real date after that day would find it due.
- **Mockup not compared:** the mockup file named in the spec (`imports/...v2.html`) is not in the repo, so the Retention tab follows the existing tool-denials table pattern. It has not been compared against the mockup or screenshotted.</result>

I read the whole diff, all of `backend/tests/test_purge.py`, `backend/tests/test_retention_api.py`, the alert-job tests in `backend/tests/test_tool_gateway_unauthorized.py` and the backend job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. CI sets both `PSA_DATABASE_URL` and `PSA_MIGRATIONS_DATABASE_URL`, so the DB-backed purge tests do run normally rather than skip.

### Platform rows linked to an Opportunity only through a workflow run are never tested

- **Changed surface:** `_purge_platform_rows` deletes trace events, model calls and tool calls either by `opportunity_id` or by a run of that Opportunity (`TraceEvent.workflow_run_id.in_(run_ids)`, `PlatformModelCall.run_id.in_(run_ids)`, `PlatformToolCall.run_id.in_(run_ids)`). The run ids are collected by `registry.run_id_providers()` before any step runs, in `_purge_one` (`backend/app/platform/purge/job.py`, new file, around lines 100â€“145). The provider is registered in `backend/app/modules/workflows/application/purge.py` (`register_run_ids`).
- **Impacted consumer or site:** the `platform.purge` job's per-Opportunity delete. This matters because `platform_model_calls.opportunity_id` and `platform_trace_events.opportunity_id` can be null (`app/platform/model_gateway/models.py:36`, `app/platform/trace/models.py:33`), so a row can belong to a run without naming the Opportunity.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. The seeder `seed_opportunity` (`backend/tests/test_purge.py` around diff lines 2466â€“2473) writes the Opportunity's id into every `opportunity_id` column and the run id into every `run_id` / `workflow_run_id` column. Every seeded platform row therefore matches the `opportunity_id` branch on its own. `test_a_due_lost_opportunity_is_purged_entirely_and_others_are_untouched` asserts nothing seeded remains and `counts["platform"] >= 4`, but no row in that test is linked by run id alone.
- **Missing verification:** a seeded trace event, model call or tool call with `opportunity_id` null (or another Opportunity's id) and `run_id` / `workflow_run_id` set to the purged Opportunity's run, followed by an assertion that it is deleted.
- **Demonstration:** any of these would pass every test I read:
  - drop the `.in_(run_ids)` alternative from any of the three deletes;
  - drop `register_run_ids(purge.run_ids)`;
  - collect run ids after the steps run (by then `workflows_runs` is already empty).
- **Consequence:** model, tool and trace records tied to a purged Opportunity's runs survive the purge, so retention is incomplete and nothing fails.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add to `test_purge.py` a case that inserts a `platform_model_calls` row and a `platform_trace_events` row with `opportunity_id` NULL and the seeded `run_id`, then asserts both are gone after `_run`.

### The "purge could not run" alert on the last attempt is never tested

- **Changed surface:** in `purge()` (`backend/app/platform/purge/job.py`), the `except Exception:` branch around `run_purge` calls `_alert(ctx, [], 0)` when `last_attempt` is true, then re-raises.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** the operator alert path. When the purge role cannot connect or the selector fails, this branch should queue a `purge_failed` alert with `failed_count == 0`, which `purge_alert_email` renders as "[PSA] The retention purge could not run".
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`. In `test_purge.py`:
  - `test_one_failure_rolls_back_only_that_opportunity_and_the_job_retries_then_alerts` covers only the per-Opportunity failure (`report.failed`); `run_purge` returns normally there.
  - `test_the_purge_alert_email_holds_counts_and_uuids_only` renders the `failed_count=0` email from a hand-built payload, but never runs the job.
  - No test makes `run_purge` or `due_opportunities` raise. I read all tests in the file.
- **Missing verification:** run `purge_job.purge` on the last attempt (e.g. `_ctx(engine, 3)`) with a failing selector or a bad purge URL. Assert that a `platform.alert_email` job with `kind = 'purge_failed'` and `failed_count = 0` is queued and that the original exception propagates.
- **Demonstration:** remove the `if last_attempt: await _alert(ctx, [], 0)` lines, or invert `last_attempt`, and every test still passes.
- **Consequence:** a purge that can never run (wrong `PSA_PURGE_DATABASE_URL`, or a role without login) goes dead with no alert, so data quietly stays past its retention date.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add a `test_purge.py` test that monkeypatches `registry.selector` (or `due_opportunities`) to raise, calls `_handle(..., attempt=3, ...)`, and asserts the queued alert payload and the re-raised error.

### The handled failure when deleting a blob file is never tested

- **Changed surface:** `_delete_blobs` (`backend/app/platform/purge/job.py`) catches `OSError` from `store.delete`, logs `purge.blob_delete_failed` and continues. This runs after the Opportunity's transaction has committed.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** `purge_opportunity` â†’ `run_purge`. The catch is what keeps an already-committed purge from being reported as failed and retried.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap` (an untested handled failure). The only "missing blob" case in `test_a_due_lost_opportunity_is_purged_entirely_and_others_are_untouched` (`_file(..., on_disk=False)`) never reaches the `except`. `BlobStore.delete` goes through `_unlink_quietly` (`app/platform/storage.py:123`), which already suppresses `FileNotFoundError`. - **Missing verification:** monkeypatch `BlobStore.delete` to raise `PermissionError`, then assert:
  - the Opportunity is in `report.purged`, not `report.failed`;
  - its rows are gone and one `platform.purge.completed` event exists;
  - the `ref_count` stays at 0.
- **Demonstration:** remove the `try/except OSError` (or narrow it to `FileNotFoundError`) and every test still passes. In real use a permission error after commit would then put an already-purged Opportunity into `report.failed`, raise `PurgeIncompleteError`, retry, and on the last attempt send a false "not purged" alert.
- **Consequence:** false failure reports and retries for Opportunities that were in fact purged.
- **Disposition:** `patch`. Add that monkeypatched-`store.delete` case to `test_purge.py`.

## Other findings

- `_alert` caps the alert at the first 50 ids with `failed[:MAX_LISTED_IDS]`, and `PurgeFailedAlert.failed_opportunity_ids` enforces `Field(max_length=MAX_LISTED_IDS)`. No test has more than 50 failures. If that slice is dropped, building `PurgeFailedAlert` raises a `ValidationError` inside `_alert`. That replaces `PurgeIncompleteError` and no alert is queued, which is exactly the many-failures case where the alert matters most. A test with 51+ failed ids calling `_alert` (or `purge` on the last attempt) would pin it.</result>

    """Make the next run work from a selection taken now (before the test changes things)."""

    async def select() -> list[RetentionDue]:
        engine = purge_engine(purge_url)
        try:

    assert {d.opportunity_id for d in selected} == set(ids)

Assumptions from the template's "Lists" sheet, so the Reports tab and the drill-down to the
failed Assumption (Stories 10.3, 10.4) have something to show. Every other line lands within
a few percent of its estimate. The output is a normal .xlsx you upload through
Actuals > Import from file.

Only openpyxl is needed (it is already in the backend venv).

"""Platform roles.

Roles are assigned in Auth0 (RBAC) and reach the API in the access token's namespaced roles
claim. Each value must equal the Auth0 role name exactly; a role in the token that is not
listed here is ignored. Roles drive the resource-scoped rules (owner/collaborator grants
and the sales-representative exclusions) and landing pages; what a role may do on its own
is the set of Auth0 permissions given to it.
"""

    ENGINEERING_REVIEWER = "engineering_reviewer"
    PM_REVIEWER = "pm_reviewer"
    SECURITY_REVIEWER = "security_reviewer"
    COMMERCIAL = "commercial"
    DELIVERY_MANAGER = "delivery_manager"
    HEAD_OF_DELIVERY = "head_of_delivery"
    PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATOR = "platform_administrator"

An Opportunity's owner can now record whether it was won or lost, from a new **Outcome** card on the Overview tab. The card shows how long the Opportunity's data will be kept.

- **Close as lost** (`POST /opportunities/{id}/outcome`, `outcome: "lost"`, optional reason): the status becomes **Closed**, and data is kept for 3 years from the date the outcome was recorded.

# Pre-Sales Agent

Agentic AI Presales Platform. A modular monolith: one Python backend (run as `api` and
`worker`), one Next.js web app, Postgres 18 with pgvector, all on Docker Compose. The
architecture is defined in
`_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-pre-sales-agent-2026-10-01/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md`.

## Layout

```text
compose.yaml          local stack (postgres, api, web); prod services arrive in Story 1.2
.env.example          local settings template (copy to .env, never commit .env)
backend/              FastAPI app, uv project (Python 3.13)
  app/modules/        business modules, each with api/ application/ domain/ adapters/
  app/orchestration/  LangGraph graphs (the only package allowed to import langgraph)
  app/agents/         proposal-only agents
  app/platform/       config, errors (problem+json), logging (JSON), db, ...
  app/main_api.py     api process (HTTP only)
  app/main_worker.py  worker process (jobs only; placeholder until Epic 2)
